items.title: BMT transport constraint and restricted-ansatz algebra
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure supplied by the GR items below. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with its metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, let $c>0$, and let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve parametrized by proper time $\tau$, with $U=D_\tau z$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $F_\tau$ be a continuous alternating two-form along $z$. Define $F^\sharp_\tau$ by
$$g(F^\sharp_\tau(v),w)=F_\tau(w,v).$$
Then $F^\sharp_\tau$ is skew-adjoint with respect to $g$.

For constants $\alpha,a,b\in\mathbb R$, consider the restricted linear transport equations
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left(aF^\sharp(s)+\frac{b}{c^2}U\,\kappa\right),\qquad \kappa:=g(s,F^\sharp(U)).$$
For every initial $s(\tau_0)$ there is a unique solution on each compact subinterval of $I$. Along any such solution,
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(U,s)=\alpha(1-a-b)\kappa.$$
Consequently, the orthogonality constraint $g(U,s)=0$ is preserved when $a+b=1$, and on that constraint $g(s,s)$ is constant. For the coefficient comparison, fix a parameter value $\tau$ and put $n:=U(\tau)/c$. Then $n$ is an observer at $z(\tau)$ and its rest space is the three-dimensional positive-definite subspace $E_\tau:=n^\perp=U(\tau)^\perp$ (the observer and projection conventions are those of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]] and [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]). Choose an orientation of $E_\tau$ and a positively oriented orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; set $e_0:=n$. For $v\in E_\tau$, write $\mathbf v=(g(v,e_1),g(v,e_2),g(v,e_3))$, use $(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$, and define $\mathbf B$ by $F_{ij}:=F(e_i,e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $P_U(v):=v+g(U,v)U/c^2$, the projection onto $E_\tau$. The rest-space matching condition means the pointwise equality
$$\bigl(P_U(D_\tau s)\bigr)^i=\alpha G\,(\mathbf s\times\mathbf B)_i\qquad(i=1,2,3)$$
for every $\mathbf s,\mathbf B$, when $s(\tau)\in E_\tau$. Thus it compares spatial components of the covariant derivative at the event, not the derivative of components in an unspecified moving tetrad. For $\alpha\ne0$, if the coefficients both preserve $g(U,s)=0$ for every initially orthogonal datum and every allowed alternating field and satisfy this matching condition, then $a=G$ and $b=1-G$. Conversely, these coefficients satisfy both requirements. This uniqueness is only within the displayed two-term ansatz; no uniqueness among all covariant spin-transport laws is asserted. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-space matching condition does not identify $a$ or $b$.

items.title: Positive-energy spin–size inequality
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Fix $c>0$ and a future unit observer $n$ in an affine Minkowski spacetime as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. Identify the positive-definite rest space $n^\perp$ isometrically with $\mathbb R^3$, with its Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$ and Lebesgue measure $d^3x$. Define the closed Euclidean ball by
$$\overline B_\ell(0):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|\le\ell\}.$$
Let $e:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable with $e\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$, and let $j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be measurable with each component $j_i\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ for $i=1,2,3$. Thus $j$ is vector-valued integrable and every vector integral below is the componentwise Lebesgue integral. Assume $e$ and $j$ are both zero almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(0)$ for some $\ell>0$, and that $|j(x)|\le e(x)/c$ almost everywhere. Define
$$E_0:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e(x)\,d^3x>0,\qquad M:=E_0/c^2,\qquad \mathbf s_*:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}x\times j(x)\,d^3x.$$
Then $\mathbf s_*$ is absolutely integrable and
$$|\mathbf s_*|\le\ell Mc,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \ell\ge\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc}.$$
The hypotheses are the full mathematical content of this estimate; it is not a bound for a quantum point particle or for a source whose energy density or momentum density fails them.

items.title: Finite-size charge multipole remainder
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $\ell>0$, $z\in\mathbb R^3$, write $d^3y$ for three-dimensional Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$, and interpret $L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ relative to this measure. Define the closed Euclidean ball
$$\overline B_\ell(z):=\{y\in\mathbb R^3:|y-z|\le\ell\},$$
using the norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and zero almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(z)$. Write $\|\rho\|_1:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\rho(y)|\,d^3y$. Let $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B_\ell(z)\subset\mathcal U$, and let $b:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^2$ for a finite integer $m\ge1$. For each component $b_k$, let
$$M_k:=\sup_{x\in\overline B_\ell(z)}\|D^2b_k(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty,$$
where, for a real bilinear map $B:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, define explicitly $\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup\{|B[u,v]|:|u|\le1,\ |v|\le1\}$ using the Euclidean vector norm. This norm is finite, and the continuous Hessian coefficients on the compact ball make each $M_k$ finite. Bilinearity gives $|B[u,v]|\le\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}|u||v|$ for all $u,v$. Define $Q:=\int\rho\,d^3y$, $d:=\int(y-z)\rho(y)\,d^3y$, and $\mathcal B:=\int\rho(y)b(y)\,d^3y$, with all three integrals over $\overline B_\ell(z)$ and vector integrals taken componentwise. Then
$$\mathcal B_k=Q\,b_k(z)+Db_k(z)d+R_k,\qquad |R_k|\le\frac12M_k\ell^2\|\rho\|_1\quad(k=1,\ldots,m).$$
Thus every fixed component in a smooth finite-component trivialization has the stated charge multipole remainder. A tensor-valued component may be treated only after a fixed smooth trivialization over the ball; derivatives of that trivialization enter $M_k$, and no covariant tensor remainder without this data is asserted.

items.title: Exact flat centroid translation and disk
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space, with signature $(-+++)$, and fix $c>0$. Let $p$ be any future timelike vector and define $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(p,p)}/c>0$. Choose an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] with $e_0=p/(Mc)$, so its ordered orthonormal basis is future and positively oriented and $p$ has components $(Mc,\mathbf 0)$ in this frame. Its positive-definite rest space is $e_0^\perp=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; use $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ for spatial components and the induced right-handed symbol $\epsilon_{ijk}$. Let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ satisfy the momentum supplementary condition $S^{ab}p_b=0$, and set $s_*^k:=\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}S^{ij}$ in this oriented orthonormal rest-space basis. Every future unit observer has the components
$$n=\gamma\left(e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{v^i}{c}e_i\right),\qquad \gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2},\qquad |\mathbf v|<c,$$
by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. For every such observer, define
$$\delta^a:=\frac{S^{ab}n_b}{p\cdot n},\qquad S'^{ab}:=S^{ab}-(\delta^ap^b-\delta^bp^a).$$
Then $p\cdot n\ne0$, $\delta\cdot p=\delta\cdot n=0$, and $S'^{ab}n_b=0$. If the representative point changes by $z\mapsto z+\delta$, the total angular momentum $J=z\wedge p+S$ is unchanged by this stipulated spin-shift rule. In the rest space,
$$\boldsymbol\delta=\frac{\mathbf s_*\times\mathbf v}{Mc^2},$$
If $\mathbf s_*\ne0$, the shifts of all future timelike observers fill the open disk in $\mathbf s_*^\perp$ of radius $|\mathbf s_*|/(Mc)$; the boundary is a supremum and is not attained. If $\mathbf s_*=0$, only the zero shift occurs. This is an exact affine-flat algebraic result.

items.title: Differentiated SSC momentum–velocity identity
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice as inherited by the supplied Lorentzian smooth-structure and connection results. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline in a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$, parametrized by proper time in the convention of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Set $U:=dz/d\tau$, so $g(U,U)=-c^2$. For finite regularity, a $C^1$ tensor field along $z$ means a tensor in the fibre over $z(\tau)$ whose components in every smooth chart are $C^1$ functions of $\tau$. Define its derivative in that chart by differentiating each component and adding $+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z)U^b$ on each upper index and $-\Gamma^c{}_{ba}(z)U^b$ on each lower index. In particular,
$$(D_\tau V)^a=\dot V^a+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z)U^bV^c,\qquad (D_\tau n)_a=\dot n_a-\Gamma^c{}_{ba}(z)U^bn_c,$$
$$(D_\tau S)^{ab}=\dot S^{ab}+\Gamma^a{}_{cd}(z)U^cS^{db}+\Gamma^b{}_{cd}(z)U^cS^{ad}.$$
These formulas extend the smooth-curve derivative of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] to the stated $C^2/C^1$ data. Let $p$ be a $C^1$ vector field along $z$, let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ and $\mathcal T^{ab}=-\mathcal T^{ab}$ be $C^1$ bivector fields along $z$, and let $n$ be a $C^1$ future unit timelike field along $z$. Suppose
$$S^{ab}n_b=0,\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a+\mathcal T^{ab}.$$
Define $\gamma:=-g(n,U)/c$ and $E_n:=-c\,g(p,n)$. Then $\gamma>0$, and
$$c\gamma\,p^a=\frac{E_n}{c}U^a+S^{ab}D_\tau n_b+\mathcal T^{ab}n_b.$$
Here $\mathcal T$ denotes an arbitrary antisymmetric torque; setting it to zero gives the torque-free case.

items.title: Admissible TD pole-dipole local closure
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-compatible Levi–Civita connection. Use SI units: coordinates are metres, proper time is seconds, $c>0$ is in metres per second, $p$ is in kilogram metres per second, $S$ is in kilogram metres squared per second, and $R$ has inverse-square-metre components. Let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline parametrized by proper time, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. For $C^1$ tensor fields along this $C^2$ curve, use the chart-independent derivative defined in [[lem-rpm-ssc-momentum-identity]]: differentiate the components, add $+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z)U^b$ on each upper index, and add $-\Gamma^c{}_{ba}(z)U^b$ on each lower index. It obeys the product and contraction rules and $D_\tau g=0$, as proved there. Let $p$ be a $C^1$ future timelike vector field along $z$, let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ be a $C^1$ bivector field, and suppose the displayed evolution equations hold:

$$D_\tau p^a=f^a:=-\frac12R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.\tag{1}$$

Put $\mu:=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}>0$, $m:=-g(p,U)/c^2>0$, $C^a:=S^{ab}p_b$, and define the linear map

$$K^a{}_b:=\mu^2\delta^a_b-\frac12S^{ac}R_{cbde}S^{de}.$$

At every state where $K$ is invertible and $W:=K^{-1}p$ is future timelike, the TD condition $C=0$ and (1) imply

$$KU=mc^2p,\qquad U=\frac{cW}{\sqrt{-g(W,W)}}.\tag{2}$$

Conversely, on the open state region where $p$ and $W$ are future timelike and $K$ is invertible, the normalized formula for $U$ in (2), together with (1), defines a smooth local ODE. A solution initialized with $C=0$ preserves $C=0$. While it remains in that admissible region, $\mu$ and $S_{ab}S^{ab}/2$ are constant. If $S=0$, then $p=(\mu/c)U$, $D_\tau p=0$, and $D_\tau U=0$. These are local statements; no continuation past loss of invertibility of $K$ or timelikeness of $W$ is asserted. Equations (1) are hypotheses of this mathematical lemma, not a physical derivation of a stress-energy moment model.

items.title: Body moments and transport convention
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Use the charged/spinning body-model conventions of the now-authored batch-24 carrier [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ in metres, $c>0$, and a $C^2$ future timelike representative curve $z:I\to M$ parametrized by proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The actual supplier defines these quantities and the SI electromagnetic-tensor convention used here. Assume Countable Choice for the GR smooth-structure, convex-normal and parallel-transport suppliers used below.

**(a) Flat isolated-body moments.** Choose an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ as in [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], with the SI coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]. Thus $e_0$ is future unit timelike and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the positively oriented orthonormal spatial basis. Let $T$ be a $C^\infty$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on the affine Minkowski spacetime $A$, whose chart components $T^{ab}$ are the model stress-energy densities with units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and have spatially compact support on every finite time slab. At a fixed time $t$, the spatial slice has coordinates $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$ and Lebesgue measure $d^3x$; define
$$p^a(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}T^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\,d^3x,$$
and, for a representative point $z(t)$ on that time slice, define
$$S_z^{ab}(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}\left((x-z(t))^aT^{0b}(ct,\mathbf x)-(x-z(t))^bT^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\right)d^3x.$$
Here $(x-z(t))^0=0$ on the chosen slice, $p$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $S_z$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. These are definitions of moments; no conservation is asserted by clause (a).

**(b) Local curved-body moments.** Let $z\in M$ and let $U_0$ be a convex normal neighborhood containing $z$. Let $\Sigma\subset U_0$ be a $C^1$ embedded spacelike hypersurface through $z$: each tangent space $T_x\Sigma$ is three-dimensional and the restriction of $g_x$ to it is positive definite. Let $n_x$ be its continuous future unit normal, so $g_x(n_x,n_x)=-1$ and $g_x(n_x,w)=0$ for every $w\in T_x\Sigma$, and let $d\Sigma$ be the positive volume measure induced by $g|_{T\Sigma}$. Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $U_0$; only its restriction $T|_\Sigma$ is used. With $(n_x)_b:=g_{bc}(x)n_x^c$, define
$$\operatorname{supp}_\Sigma(T|_\Sigma):=\overline{\{x\in\Sigma:T_x\ne0\}}^{\,\Sigma}.$$
Assume this restricted support is a compact subset of $U_0$ and that all displayed integrands are absolutely integrable with respect to $d\Sigma$. For every $x\in\Sigma$, let $v(x):=\exp_z^{-1}(x)\in T_zM$ be the unique joining position vector supplied by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] and [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $H_{x\to z}:T_xM\to T_zM$ be parallel transport along that unique geodesic, with existence, uniqueness and metric preservation as in [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]. Define $T^\sharp(n_x)^a:=T^{ab}(x)(n_x)_b$ and
$$p_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,\qquad S_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma v(x)\wedge H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,$$
where $(v\wedge w)^{ab}:=v^aw^b-v^bw^a$ and the finite-dimensional vector and tensor integrals are taken componentwise in any basis of $T_zM$. The resulting $p_z$ and $S_z$ are a vector and an antisymmetric tensor at $z$; their units are $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. “Support on $\Sigma$” here means only compact support of the restriction $T|_\Sigma$; it does not assert that the ambient smooth field $T$ has spacetime support contained in $\Sigma$.

items.title: Pole-dipole and closed multipole test-body models
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice as inherited from [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. For a neutral test body, let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve parametrized by proper time, let $U=dz/d\tau$, and let $p^a$ and $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ be the momentum and spin moments of [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. Adopt the pole-dipole evolution equations
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12 R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.$$
A spin-supplementary condition (SSC) is an additional equation $S^{ab}n_b=0$ for a specified future unit timelike field $n$ along $z$; this postulate does not select one SSC, and $p$ is an independently evolved moment rather than a primitive assumption $p=mU$.

For a retained quadrupole or higher-multipole model, adopt
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12 R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd}+f_{\rm extra}^a,\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a+N_{\rm extra}^{ab},$$
where $f_{\rm extra}$ is a specified smooth force map along the state and $N_{\rm extra}^{ab}=-N_{\rm extra}^{ba}$ is a specified smooth torque map. A quadrupole convention that may be adopted is
$$f_{\rm quad}^a=-\frac16J^{bcde}\nabla^aR_{bcde},\qquad N_{\rm quad}^{ab}=\frac43R^{[a}{}_{cde}J^{b]cde},$$
with $J^{bcde}$ satisfying the algebraic symmetries of the curvature tensor, carrying units $\mathrm{kg\,m^4\,s^{-2}}$, and brackets including the factor $1/2$. Any evolved $J$ or higher moment needs its own transport or constitutive law; without it the multipole equations are not a closed initial-value model.

The pole-dipole and multipole equations are adopted finite-dimensional truncations, not derivations from the moment integrals above. Their use as approximations for a material body is restricted to regimes in which its size is small compared with the relevant curvature and background-variation lengths and omitted moment effects are negligible on the stated finite interval. These conditions are qualitative applicability assumptions here: this postulate supplies no uniform error bound, no convergence of truncations, and no global existence claim. No experimental result or measurement is asserted.

items.title: BMT orthogonality and conserved spin length
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Adopt the charged-body quantities and SI tensor convention of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], the polarization transport postulate [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]], and its translational equation obtained from [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. On a local potential domain, assume the finite curve segments are stationary for the adopted action. Let $z$ be a $C^2$ future timelike proper-time curve, $U=dz/d\tau$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, with prescribed continuous alternating field $F$ along it. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $g_s\in\mathbb R$, and an initial $C^1$ spin vector satisfy $g(s,U)=0$. Put $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, and $\kappa=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$. The adopted equations and action result give

$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left[G F^\sharp(s)+(1-G)\frac{U}{c^2}\kappa\right].$$

Then $g(s,U)=0$ and $g(s,s)$ are constant along every solution. In the restricted ansatz $D_\tau s=\alpha[aF^\sharp(s)+bU\kappa/c^2]$, require preservation of orthogonality for every initially orthogonal datum and every allowed alternating field. For $\alpha\ne0$ this gives $a+b=1$. If, in addition, the pointwise projected rest-space matching condition of [[lem-rpm-bmt-transport-algebra]] holds with target coefficient $G$, that lemma gives $a=G$, and hence $b=1-G$. This coefficient conclusion is only within that ansatz and the stated joint conditions. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-space matching condition does not identify $a,b$.

items.title: Spherical charge exterior-energy size bound
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let an extended static spherical charged body have radius $\ell>0$ metres, total charge $q\in\mathbb R$ coulombs, and finite total rest energy $Mc^2$ with $M>0$ kilograms. Use the flat-body moment convention of [[def-rpm-body-moments]] in a momentum-rest inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], with $p=Mc\,e_0$ and $o$ the stipulated center of the spherical body. Its rest spatial chart has coordinates $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$; define $r:=|\mathbf x|:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$, $\widehat{\mathbf r}:=\mathbf x/r$ for $r>0$, and $\overline B_\ell(0):=\{\mathbf x:r\le\ell\}$. The body support lies in $\overline B_\ell(0)$, and $\ell$ is the radius of the specified exterior region. Use the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], including $c$ in metres per second and $\varepsilon_0>0$. On the open exterior spatial region $\Omega_\ell:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3:r>\ell\}$, the static field is assumed to obey
$$\mathbf E(\mathbf x)=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2}\widehat{\mathbf r},\qquad \mathbf B=0.$$
Let $u(\mathbf x)$ be the time-independent vacuum energy density of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] on this exterior region and define $E_{\rm ext}:=\int_{\Omega_\ell}u(\mathbf x)\,d^3x$. Assume the total rest energy is the sum of this exterior field energy and a remaining material-plus-interior contribution $E_{\rm rem}\ge0$. Then
$$Mc^2\ge\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\ell},\qquad \ell\ge\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0Mc^2}.$$
The exact Coulomb exterior and nonnegative energy accounting are hypotheses. The theorem does not infer an exterior field from spherical symmetry alone. No identification of field energy with an ideal point particle's rest mass is made.

items.title: SSC choices and hidden momentum
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume the neutral pole-dipole equations adopted in [[post-rpm-mpd-truncation]] for the local moments of [[def-rpm-body-moments]]: along a $C^2$ future timelike proper-time curve $z$, with $U=dz/d\tau$, $p$ future timelike and $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$,
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.$$
For any $C^1$ future unit observer field $n$ along the curve satisfying the SSC $S^{ab}n_b=0$, put $\gamma=-g(n,U)/c>0$ and $E_n=-cg(p,n)$. Then
$$c\gamma p^a=\frac{E_n}{c}U^a+S^{ab}D_\tau n_b.$$
In the Pirani branch $n=U/c$, define $m=-g(p,U)/c^2>0$ and $a=D_\tau U$; then
$$p^a=mU^a+\frac{1}{c^2}S^{ab}a_b.$$
In the parallel-observer (OKS) branch $D_\tau n=0$, $p$ is a positive scalar multiple of $U$. In the TD branch $n=p/\mu$, $\mu=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}$, define $m:=-g(p,U)/c^2>0$ as in the Pirani branch. The derivative term generally remains and the identity gives $mc^2p=\mu^2U+S D_\tau p$; it does not by itself imply $p\parallel U$.

items.title: Rest-frame spin transport and finite-body size bounds
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Adopt the charged-body quantities of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the SI field convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the classical BMT law [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]]. For a trajectory stationary under the local action postulate, the translational force equation is supplied by [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. In flat Minkowski spacetime let $m>0$, $q,g_s\in\mathbb R$, $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, and let $U,s$ satisfy
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left[GF^\sharp(s)-(G-1)\frac{U}{c^2}g(s,F^\sharp(U))\right],\qquad g(U,U)=-c^2,\quad g(U,s)=0.$$
The tensor equation is covariant under proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations of the complete field and worldline data. If $F=0$, then $D_\tau U=0$ and $D_\tau s=0$. For any acceleration $a=D_\tau U$ within the Lorentz-force model, the $G=0$ branch is Fermi–Walker transport on the orthogonal spin subspace:
$$D_\tau s=\frac{1}{c^2}\bigl(Ug(a,s)-a g(U,s)\bigr)=\frac{U}{c^2}g(a,s).$$
For the uniform-field branch, choose an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] with $e_0=U/c$ for the stationary trajectory and with the positively oriented orthonormal spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Let $\mathbf E=0$ and let the constant spatial field be $\mathbf B\ne0$; its norm and cross product are those of the frame's positive-definite spatial structure. Then $U=(c,\mathbf0)$ is stationary, $\widehat{\mathbf B}:=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$, and for $\mathbf s_0:=\mathbf s(\tau_0)$ define $\mathbf s_{\parallel,0}:=(\mathbf s_0\cdot\widehat{\mathbf B})\widehat{\mathbf B}$ and $\mathbf s_{\perp,0}:=\mathbf s_0-\mathbf s_{\parallel,0}$. The $G$ branch has the exact solution
$$\mathbf s(\tau)=\mathbf s_{\parallel,0}+\cos(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf s_{\perp,0}-\sin(\omega\Delta\tau)\widehat{\mathbf B}\times\mathbf s_{\perp,0},\qquad \omega=\frac{qG}{m}|\mathbf B|,\quad \Delta\tau=\tau-\tau_0.$$
The $F=0$, $G=0$, and uniform-field claims are deductions within the adopted model, not experimental statements. For the independent finite-body branch, use the moment and unit convention of [[def-rpm-body-moments]]; the density-to-spin identity below is stipulated data.

Separately, let a flat body have rest momentum $p$, and define $M:=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}/c>0$. Choose its momentum-rest inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] with $e_0=p/(Mc)$ and spatial origin at the stipulated body center. Define $\overline B_\ell(0):=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3:|\mathbf x|\le\ell\}$ using the Euclidean norm of its positive-definite spatial rest space. In this frame $p$ has components $(Mc,\mathbf0)$; let $S^{ab}=-S^{ba}$ be its angular-momentum tensor, with $S^{0i}=0$ (hence $S^{ab}p_b=0$), and let $e:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ and $j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be measurable rest densities, with each component of $j$ in $L^1(\mathbb R^3)$; their units are joules per cubic metre and kilogram per square metre per second, respectively. Assume $e$ and $j$ vanish almost everywhere outside $\overline B_\ell(0)$, $|j|$ is the Euclidean norm and satisfies $|j|\le e/c$ almost everywhere, $\int e\,d^3x=Mc^2$, and the stipulated componentwise spin-density identity
$$\mathbf s_*:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf x\times j(\mathbf x)\,d^3x=\tfrac12\epsilon_{kij}S^{ij}\,\mathbf e_k,$$
where the vector integral is componentwise in the positively oriented spatial basis of this inertial frame.
Then
$$\ell\ge\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc},\qquad |\boldsymbol\delta|<\frac{|\mathbf s_*|}{Mc}$$
for every observer-induced centroid shift $\boldsymbol\delta$ of the flat SSC translation law; the disk radius is a supremum, not an attained boundary for a timelike observer. These rest-body quantities are Lorentz invariant under transforming the complete body data and its momentum-rest hypersurface. No equality between $\mathbf s$ and $\mathbf s_*$ is assumed, so the size inequalities do not bound the BMT polarization unless such an identification is separately adopted.

items.title: TD spin and momentum norms
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Adopt the neutral pole-dipole equations and local body moments of [[post-rpm-mpd-truncation]] and [[def-rpm-body-moments]]. Suppose a solution satisfies the TD condition $S^{ab}p_b=0$, with future timelike $p$, and remains in the local admissible region of [[lem-rpm-td-local-closure]] where $K$ is invertible and $W=K^{-1}p$ is future timelike. Then, on its local interval of existence,
$$\mu:=\sqrt{-g(p,p)}\quad\text{and}\quad \frac12S_{ab}S^{ab}$$
are constant. If the initial spin tensor is zero, it remains zero and the solution obeys
$$p=\frac{\mu}{c}U,\qquad D_\tau p=0,\qquad D_\tau U=0,$$
so the representative curve is a timelike geodesic with constant rest mass $M=\mu/c$. The claims stop if the local TD admissible region ends; no global extension follows.

items.title: BMT G=0 Fermi–Walker and G=1 shared-generator cases
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Use the charged-body conventions and adopted BMT transport equation of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] and [[post-rpm-bmt-dipole-model]]. On a local potential domain, take the trajectory stationary under the action postulate so that [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] supplies its translation equation. Let $U$ be future timelike, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $g(U,s)=0$. Write $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, $\kappa=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$, and $a=D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U)$. The BMT law is
$$D_\tau s=\alpha\left[GF^\sharp(s)-(G-1)\frac{U\kappa}{c^2}\right].$$

(a) If $g_s=0$ ($G=0$), then $D_\tau s=Ug(a,s)/c^2$, the Fermi–Walker transport law on $U^\perp$.

(b) If $g_s=2$ ($G=1$), then $D_\tau s=\alpha F^\sharp(s)$ while $D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U)$, so the same linear field operator transports both vectors. Both parameter cases preserve orthogonality and spin norm by [[pthm-rpm-bmt-constraints]].

items.title: Fixed-charge and scaled small-body limits
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume the static spherical-body hypotheses of [[pthm-rpm-spherical-charge-size-bound]], so every member obeys $\ell\ge q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0Mc^2)$.

(a) For fixed $q\ne0$ and fixed finite $M>0$, the lower bound is the positive constant $q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0Mc^2)$. Thus no family satisfying these hypotheses can have $\ell\to0$ while keeping both $q$ and $M$ fixed.

(b) For $q(\lambda)=\lambda q_0$, $M(\lambda)=\lambda M_0$, and $\ell(\lambda)=\lambda\ell_0$ with $\lambda>0$, $q_0\ne0$ coulombs, $M_0>0$ kilograms, and $\ell_0>0$ metres, the same necessary condition reduces to $\ell_0\ge q_0^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0M_0c^2)$, independent of $\lambda$. The inequality therefore does not rule out this scaling, although it does not construct a body family or prove that its interior energy remains admissible.

items.title: Rest magnetic spin rotation and independent centroid disk
items.design_state: Draft carrier authored in assigned batch; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle and connection suppliers used by the BMT transport and charged-action equivalence. No full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

In a charged-body inertial frame of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] with $e_0=U/c$, positively oriented spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, and constant coordinates for the stationary trajectory, let $U=(c,\mathbf0)$, $\mathbf E=0$, and $\mathbf B=B\mathbf e_3$ with constant $B>0$ tesla. Let the adopted polarization law have $q$ in coulombs, $m>0$ kilograms, $\alpha=q/m$, $G=g_s/2$, and choose initial polarization $\mathbf s(\tau_0)=s_0\mathbf e_1$ in kilogram metres squared per second. Independently, choose a separate momentum-rest inertial frame $(o';f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] with $f_0=p/(Mc)$, spatial origin $o'$ at the stipulated body center, and positive spatial basis $(f_1,f_2,f_3)$. Let a flat material body have rest momentum components $p=(Mc,\mathbf0)$ in this frame, $M>0$ kilograms, body angular momentum $\mathbf s_*=S_*f_3$ with $S_*>0$ in kilogram metres squared per second, and measurable densities $e:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ and $j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with each component of $j$ in $L^1(\mathbb R^3)$, expressed in its spatial coordinates $\mathbf x$. Define $\overline B_\ell(0):=\{\mathbf x:|\mathbf x|\le\ell\}$ using this rest-space Euclidean norm. Assume $e$ and $j$ vanish almost everywhere outside this ball for $\ell>0$ metres, $|j|$ is that norm and satisfies $|j|\le e/c$ almost everywhere, $\int e\,d^3x=Mc^2$, and the componentwise vector integral satisfies $\mathbf s_*=\int\mathbf x\times j\,d^3x$. Assume also that its spin tensor is the spatial dual of $\mathbf s_*$ and obeys the momentum SSC. Then the polarization and body-centroid results are

$$\mathbf s(\tau)=s_0\bigl(\cos(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf e_1-\sin(\omega\Delta\tau)\mathbf e_2\bigr),\qquad \omega=\frac{qGB}{m},\quad \Delta\tau=\tau-\tau_0,$$

$$\ell\ge\frac{S_*}{Mc},\qquad \boldsymbol\delta=(\delta_1,\delta_2,0)\ \text{in the body-frame spatial components},\quad \delta_1^2+\delta_2^2<\left(\frac{S_*}{Mc}\right)^2.$$

Every interior shift vector is realized by some future timelike observer. There is no identification between $s_0$ and $S_*$ in this example.
